headline: Jamaat-e-Islami: India flouts diplomatic norms by allowing Hasina press conference
summary: The party termed the move a "gross violation" of international etiquette, urging the government to seek Interpol and UN assistance to bring her back.
details: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has termed India's decision to allow fugitive former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to hold a press conference in New Delhi a "gross violation" of diplomatic norms.

Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar alleged that India is ignoring Bangladesh's diplomatic appeals by continuing to shelter Hasina and allowing her to engage in political activities from its capital.
The press conference, held on Wednesday night, coincided with the second anniversary of the July uprising, which has drawn strong resentment from the Bangladesh government.
Porwar stated that while Bangladesh seeks relations based on mutual respect and equality, New Delhi has disregarded repeated requests regarding Hasina.
The party urged the government to take more effective steps, including seeking an Interpol red notice and UN assistance to ensure her return to Bangladesh.
Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman also questioned why the government has failed to bring Hasina back despite an existing prisoner exchange agreement between the two countries.
Rahman stressed that Hasina, who has been sentenced to death in a crimes against humanity case, must return to face a fair trial in Bangladesh.
caption:
India's decision to allow Sheikh Hasina to hold a press conference in New Delhi is a "gross violation" of diplomatic norms, says Jamaat-e-Islami.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has termed India's decision to allow fugitive former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to hold a press conference in New Delhi a "gross violation" of diplomatic norms.

Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar alleged that India is ignoring Bangladesh's diplomatic appeals by continuing to shelter Hasina and allowing her to engage in political activities from its capital.

The press conference, held on Wednesday night, coincided with the second anniversary of the July uprising, which has drawn strong resentment from the Bangladesh government.

Porwar stated that while Bangladesh seeks relations based on mutual respect and equality, New Delhi has disregarded repeated requests regarding Hasina.

The party urged the government to take more effective steps, including seeking an Interpol red notice and UN assistance to ensure her return to Bangladesh.

Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman also questioned why the government has failed to bring Hasina back despite an existing prisoner exchange agreement between the two countries.

Rahman stressed that Hasina, who has been sentenced to death in a crimes against humanity case, must return to face a fair trial in Bangladesh.

headline: 867 dead as measles outbreak kills 4 more in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in measles cases and deaths across Bangladesh, with Dhaka being heavily affected.
details: Four people died from measles or measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 867 since March 15, according to the DGHS.
In the last 24 hours, 776 new cases were reported, including 99 confirmed measles cases and 677 people with measles-like symptoms.
Dhaka alone saw four deaths in the last 24 hours: two confirmed measles cases and two with measles-like symptoms.
Since March 15, 152,372 people have been affected by measles or measles-like symptoms across the country.
Of these, 17,040 cases have been laboratory-confirmed as measles, while 135,332 people showed symptoms.
Hospitalization rates are high, with 117,444 people admitted to hospitals since March 15, and 113,200 discharged.
The total death toll includes 769 deaths linked to measles-like symptoms and 98 deaths from confirmed measles cases.
